Made by mutating a $(item)Polonium Block$(0) with $(l:psitweaks_spell_pieces/trick_material_mutation)$(o)Trick: Material Mutation$(0)$(/l), or by processing it in the $(l:psitweaks_machines/material_mutator)$(o)Material Mutator$(0)$(/l).$(p)Used for the $(l:psitweaks_machines/transcendent_universal_cable)$(o)$(item)Transcendent Universal Cable$(0)$(/l) and the MekaSuit $(item)Phenomenon Interference Enhancement Unit$(0).
psi.book.page.psitweaks_material.psionic: Crafted from $(l:components/psitweaks_alloy_psion)$(o)$(item)Psionic Alloy$(0)$(/l) and a Mekanism Elite Control Circuit.$(p)Used in PsiTweaks machines, upgraded spell bullets, and similar recipes.

Made by infusing an $(item)Echo Shard$(0) with Psionic Echo infusion, or by using the $(l:psitweaks_spell_pieces/trick_supreme_infusion)$(o)Trick: Supreme Infusion$(0)$(/l).$(p)Used as the base catalyst for $(l:components/psitweaks_alloy_psionic_echo)echo-tier alloys$(/l), HDΨE materials, gas processing, and advanced psionic machinery.
psi.book.page.psitweaks_material.psycheo: Infuse $(l:components/psitweaks_heavy_psimetal)$(o)$(item)Heavy Psimetal$(0)$(/l) with Hypostasis to make $(item)Psycheonic Metal Nuggets$(0), then craft nine nuggets into an ingot.$(p)Used for $(l:items/psitweaks_spell_bullets)transcendent spell bullets$(/l), Psycheonic Metal CAD assemblies, and the highest psionic material tier.
psi.book.page.psitweaks_material.unrefin: Crafted from $(l:components/psitweaks_chaotic_psimetal)$(o)$(item)Chaotic Psimetal$(0)$(/l) and Refined Glowstone.$(p)Enrich it to obtain usable $(l:components/psitweaks_flashmetal)$(o)$(item)Flashmetal$(0)$(/l).
psi.book.page.psitweaks_mekanism_integra: $(thing)PsiTweaks$(0) ties $(thing)Psi$(0) into $(thing)Mekanism$(0) progression. Its integration covers Metallurgic Infusing recipes for Psi materials, MekaSuit modules that improve caster stats, and machines that exchange Psi, FE, and psionic resources.$(p)See JEI for exact recipes.

The $(item)Metallurgic Infuser$(0) can produce core Psi materials with PsiTweaks infuse types. Psigem infusion turns redstone into $(l:components/psidust)$(o)$(item)Psidust$(0)$(/l) and gold into $(item)Psimetal$(0).$(p)Ebony and Ivory infusion can make $(item)Ebony Substance$(0), $(item)Ivory Substance$(0), and their Psimetal variants. Later recipes extend this chain into $(l:components/psitweaks_chaotic_factor)psionic factors$(/l), $(l:components/psitweaks_chaotic_psimetal)$(o)$(item)Chaotic Psimetal$(0)$(/l), $(l:components/psitweaks_psionic_echo)Psionic Echo materials$(/l), and $(l:components/psitweaks_alloy_hypostasis)Hypostasis-tier metal$(/l).

PsiTweaks adds three MekaSuit modules for spellcasters. The $(item)Psyon Supplying Unit$(0) and $(item)Psyon Capacity Unit$(0) install in the MekaSuit body armor and improve Psi regeneration and maximum Psi.$(p)The $(item)Phenomenon Interference Enhancement Unit$(0) installs in the MekaSuit helmet and increases Phenomenon Interference.
psi.book.page.psitweaks_mode_selection.0: Some PsiTweaks spell pieces support mode selection.$(p)A mode-selectable spell piece can switch the type it handles without changing to a different piece.
psi.book.page.psitweaks_mode_selection.1: For example, List operators can switch between String List, Number List, Vector List, Item List, and Block List.$(p)The selected mode changes the input and output types of operations such as Add to List and List Concatenation.
psi.book.page.psitweaks_mode_selection.2: To choose a mode, left-click the spell piece in the Spell Programmer.$(p)The current mode appears on the piece and in its tooltip. If a connection fails, check that the piece mode matches the type of the connected value.
psi.book.page.psitweaks_overview.0: $(thing)PsiTweaks$(0) is an expansion for $(thing)Psi$(0). It adds higher-tier spell bullets, new CAD assemblies and casting support tools, new spells, processing machines, and generators.$(p)It ties Psi into industrial setups and keeps it strong for combat and utility through the late game, beyond ordinary CADs and basic spell bullets.
psi.book.page.psitweaks_programming_type: $(thing)PsiTweaks$(0) adds String, Block, Item, and Matrix types to Psi spell programming.$(p)Values split into Plain Values (Number, Vector, String, Matrix, etc.), which can be stored in CAD memory, and world-dependent Contextual Values (Entity, Block, Item, etc.).

String holds text such as IDs, names, NBT paths, and filter patterns.$(p)Runtime Strings cap at 8,192 characters, and Constant: String pieces cap at 1,024. Pattern matching (* ? [abc]) enforces a per-cast comparison limit.

Block represents a world block with its position, state, ID, tags, and name, and auto-converts with Vector and Vector List on most inputs.$(p)Item represents an ItemStack obtained from hands, inventories, or dropped items.

Matrix is a Plain Value representing a 1×1 to 4×4 numeric matrix. Like Number and Vector, it can be stored in CAD memory and converted to text.$(p)Dedicated operators build, add, multiply, slice, transpose, and invert matrices, transform vectors, and define 3D regions.
psi.book.page.psitweaks_research.0: Some spell pieces added by $(thing)PsiTweaks$(0) must be unlocked through research before they can be used in spell programs.$(p)Research creates program items that correspond to those spell pieces. Right-clicking with a program unlocks its spell piece, and the program is not consumed.
psi.book.page.psitweaks_research.1: Place the required ingredients in the $(l:psitweaks_machines/program_researcher)$(o)$(item)Program Research Table$(0)$(/l) and supply FE to craft a program.$(p)JEI lists each research recipe's required materials, energy usage per tick, and processing time.
psi.book.page.psitweaks_research.no_meka: When $(thing)Mekanism$(0) is not installed, craft a Blank Program together with the materials for the corresponding spell piece in any arrangement to create its program.$(p)Check JEI for each crafting recipe's required materials.
psi.book.page.psitweaks_spell_bullets.0: $(thing)PsiTweaks$(0) adds upgraded tiers above the ordinary $(l:items/spell_bullet)$(o)$(item)Spell Bullet$(0)$(/l): Advanced, Resonant, Sublimated, Awakened, and Transcendent.$(p)Every Psi spell bullet variant has upgraded tiers available.
psi.book.page.psitweaks_spell_bullets.1: Upgrading a spell bullet requires four bullets from the previous tier, making it very expensive.
psi.book.page.psitweaks_spell_bullets.2: Higher tiers greatly improve cost efficiency, making powerful spells easier to cast.
psi.book.page.psitweaks_spellgram_object: SpellGram objects are entities with their own integrity (Resident SpellGrams, Micro Black Holes, etc.). Opponents can wear down their integrity and destroy them with $(l:psitweaks_spell_pieces/trick_gram_demolition)Trick: Gram Demolition$(/l) or $(l:psitweaks_spell_pieces/trick_psi_bullet)Trick: Psi Bullet$(/l).$(p)Resident SpellGrams ($(l:psitweaks/zone_magic)Zone Magic$(/l), circles, Decontamination, etc.) stay active where placed. Each caster can keep up to 32, and they vanish on logout or dimension change.

Aim at a core within 5 blocks to see its name and remaining integrity.$(p)Manage your Resident SpellGrams with these pieces:$(li)$(l:psitweaks_spell_pieces/selector_own_spellgrams)Selector: Own Resident SpellGrams$(/l): get yours in the dimension as an Entity List$(li)$(l:psitweaks_spell_pieces/selector_spellgram_integrity)Selector: SpellGram Integrity$(/l) / $(l:psitweaks_spell_pieces/selector_spellgram_integrity_list)List$(/l): read remaining integrity$(li)$(l:psitweaks_spell_pieces/trick_extend_spellgram)Trick: Extend SpellGram$(/l): restore integrity$(li)$(l:psitweaks_spell_pieces/trick_recall_spellgram)Trick: Recall SpellGram$(/l): remove from any distance
psi.book.page.psitweaks_spellpiece.const: Outputs the entered string as a String value. The value is saved with the spell and is limited to 1024 characters.
psi.book.page.psitweaks_spellpiece.jump_: A marker used as the destination for Trick: Jump and Trick: Switch. This spell piece itself does nothing. You can input a constant String as its label.
psi.book.page.psitweaks_spellpiece.macro: Moves the given position by Left/Right, Forward/Backward, and Up/Down relative to the caster's horizontal facing. Facing is rounded to the nearest horizontal cardinal direction, and pitch is ignored. Positive values move right, forward, and up; negative values move the opposite way. Unconnected parameters are treated as 0. The mode button switches to vector input: a single vector whose components are distances in the caster's view frame (X = right, Y = up, Z = forward), equivalent to adding the result of Macro: Caster Axial Rotation to the position.

Like Macro: Caster Axial Offset, but the facing is rounded to the nearest of the six axis directions, including straight up and down. When looking straight up or down, forward points vertically and the Up/Down axis becomes horizontal, so offsets form a horizontal plane. This is useful for effects like 3x3 area mining, where the mined plane should become the floor or ceiling when looking up or down. The mode button switches to vector input: a single vector whose components are distances in the caster's view frame (X = right, Y = view-up, Z = forward), equivalent to adding the result of Macro: Caster Axial Rotation (3D) to the position.

Rotates the given direction vector from the caster's view frame into world space. The X component is treated as right, Y as up, and Z as forward relative to the caster's horizontal facing, which is rounded to the nearest cardinal direction; pitch is ignored. For example, (0, 0, 1) returns the caster's facing direction and (1, 0, 0) returns the direction to the caster's right. The vector's magnitude is preserved.

Like Macro: Caster Axial Rotation, but the facing is rounded to the nearest of the six axis directions, including straight up and down. The X component is treated as right, Y as view-up, and Z as forward. When looking straight up or down, Z points vertically and Y becomes horizontal, matching the orientation of the view.
Raycasts from the caster's position in the look direction and returns the coordinates of the hit block.
Raycasts from the caster's position in the look direction and returns the normal direction of the hit face.
Raycasts from the caster's position in the look direction and returns the coordinates of the hit block with a collision shape.
Raycasts from the caster's position in the look direction and returns the normal direction of the face of the hit block with a collision shape.
Raycasts from the caster's position in the look direction and returns the coordinates of the hit block or fluid.
Raycasts from the caster's position in the look direction and returns the normal direction of the face of the hit block or fluid.

Offsets a position relative to the block face hit by a raycast from the caster, using the hit block if Position is omitted.$(p)Positive values move right, inward, and up as viewed; Vector mode takes one vector with X=right, Y=up, Z=inward.
When a spell uses multiple Face Axial Offset or Rotation pieces, only the first executed performs the raycast and shares its hit block and face with the rest, even if the block breaks mid-spell.

Rotates the specified direction vector according to the orientation of the block face hit by a raycast from the caster. X points right as the face is viewed, Y points toward the top as the face is viewed, and Z points inward into the block. On the top and bottom faces, the caster's horizontal facing determines the rotation within the face. The vector's magnitude is preserved. If the raycast misses, a null-vector error is raised.

Face Axial Offset and Face Axial Rotation in the same program share the raycast result of the first one executed. See page 2 of $(l:psitweaks_spell_pieces/macro_face_axial_offset)$(o)Macro: Face Axial Offset$(0)$(/l) for details.
psi.book.page.psitweaks_spellpiece.opera: Filters the input Entity List and returns only LivingEntity instances that are currently alive.
Returns the arc tangent of the target number.

Outputs how much more a block accepts right now, by simulating an insertion; nothing moves. Everything but String works as in Operator: Block Resource Amount. String takes one exact ID such as minecraft:coal: no wildcards, "minecraft:" may be omitted, and unknown IDs read as 0.

Items are simulated slot by slot, so machines whose slots share one pool may report more than really fits. A block that accepts without limit reports a very large number. Use it to keep machines stocked, for example by withdrawing fuel from your Ideaspace Storage only while a furnace has room for it.

Outputs the item that Pick Block gives for the block, as an Item: wheat seeds for a wheat crop, and an empty Item for air. It works as an Item filter, for example in Trick: Ideaspace Storage - Slot Withdraw.
Outputs the position saved in a Block as a Vector. Pieces that take a Vector also accept a Block directly, so this is mainly for checking coordinates with Trick: Debug.
Gets the positions saved in a Block List as a Vector List. A Block List can also be connected directly to Vector List inputs, which then use these positions.

Outputs how much a block holds of the kind chosen in the mode menu: items (count), fluids or chemicals (mB), or FE. Direction picks the face to read, following the block's per-face input and output; unconnected, the whole block is read.

The optional String filters by ID with * (any text) and ? (any single character); omit the namespace, such as "minecraft:", to match across all mods. Start with # to match tags instead, such as #c:ingots. Unconnected or empty, everything is counted. Blocks with no such storage, in unloaded chunks or in other dimensions read as 0, as do chemicals without Mekanism. A protected block fails with an error.

Outputs the block state saved in a Block value as a String, using Minecraft's command-style form such as minecraft:oak_stairs[facing=north,half=bottom]. The value comes from the Block snapshot and does not change if the world changes later.

Outputs the properties saved in a Block value's block state as a String List. Each entry uses property:value form, such as facing:north or waterlogged:false. Blocks with no state properties output an empty String List.

Outputs one property value from the block state saved in a Block value. Use the String input to name a property such as facing or waterlogged. If the property does not exist, it outputs an empty String.
Returns the coordinates of the blocks of the same kind connected to the block at the position (diagonally too) as a Vector List, nearest first, up to $(thing)Max$(0) blocks (at most 4096).

Crops of any age and logs facing any way count as one kind. Blocks outside the spell's range are not followed.$(p)Pass the list to $(thing)Trick: Mass Block Break$(0) to fell a tree or mine out a vein of ore, or to $(thing)Trick: Mass Harvest$(0) to harvest a whole field.
Returns the hyperbolic cosine of the target number.
Turns the dropped items in an Entity List, such as from Selector: Nearby Items, into an Item List, keeping their order and skipping other entities.

Compares Value 1 and Value 2 as Any inputs. It outputs 1 when both values are equal, otherwise 0. Numbers compare by numeric value, Vectors compare by coordinates, Item values compare their item data and source, and Block values compare dimension, position, and block state. A Block compared with a Vector uses coordinate comparison.

Outputs a String by replacing {1}, {2}, and {3} in the saved template with up to three optional Any inputs. The template uses the same input window as Constant: String and is limited to 1024 characters. Unconnected inputs become empty text. Contextual Values such as Entity, Item, and Block use the same localized display name as Selector: Display Name. Contextual Value Lists use the same localized names as Selector: Display Name List and are joined with commas. Other values use the normal String conversion. The final output is capped by the runtime String limit.

Converts the String input for the selected Plain mode. String mode returns the input as-is. Number mode parses finite numeric text and outputs 0 on invalid input. Vector mode accepts Vector[x,y,z], Vector(x,y,z), [x,y,z], or (x,y,z), case-insensitive for Vector, and outputs the zero vector when parsing fails.

Outputs the registry ID of a Contextual Value as a String. Entity inputs output the EntityType ID, Item inputs output the Item ID, and Block inputs output the Block ID. Unsupported contextual values output an empty String.

Outputs registry IDs from a Contextual Value List as a String List. Entity List, Item List, and Block List preserve their input order. Vector List input is converted to Block List by reading the blocks at those world coordinates. Unsupported or empty elements become empty strings.
Compares Value 1 and Value 2 as Numbers. It outputs 1 when Value 1 is greater than Value 2, otherwise 0.
Compares Value 1 and Value 2 as Numbers. It outputs 1 when Value 1 is greater than or equal to Value 2, otherwise 0.

Filters a list and returns only the elements inside the parallelepiped defined by a 3x4 or 4x4 matrix. The first three columns are the edge vectors and the fourth column is the start point. Points exactly on the boundary are counted as inside.

Choose the list type in the mode menu. Entity (default) tests the center of each bounding box, Vector tests each vector as given, and Block tests block positions, the same points Operator: Region Vector List returns.
Outputs the stack count of an Item value as a Number. Empty Item values output 0.

Outputs the zero-based inventory slot number saved in an Item value. Items obtained from entity or block inventory slots retain this source slot. Items without an inventory-slot source, including empty Items, hand or equipment Items, and dropped item entities, output -1.

Outputs the total stack count from an Item List. If the String input is empty or not connected, all Items are counted. Otherwise only Items whose registry ID exactly matches the String are counted. Invalid IDs simply match nothing and output 0.
Adds up to three elements to the List.
Combines the two input Lists. For Contextual Value Lists, duplicate elements are removed.

Sorts the elements of the selected List mode (Entity, Vector or Block) by their distance from the position, closest first, and returns the element at the Number. Counting starts at 0: 0 is the closest element and 1 the next. A negative Number counts from the farthest, so -1 is the farthest element. A Number outside the List is an error. Entities are measured at their feet, so 0 gives the same entity as Operator: Closest to Point; blocks are measured at their center.

Sorts the elements of the selected List mode (Entity, Vector or Block) by their distance from the position and keeps some of them. A positive Number keeps that many of the closest, a negative Number keeps the farthest, and 0 gives an empty List. Vector and Block Lists come out closest first (farthest first for a negative Number). An Entity List always keeps Psi's own order, so only which entities remain changes. Entities are measured at their feet, as in Operator: Closest to Point, and blocks at their center.
Returns a new List by removing elements from List 1 when they are also present in List 2.

Converts a String List for the selected Plain mode. String mode returns the input list as-is. Number mode parses each entry as finite numeric text, so invalid entries become 0. Vector mode converts only entries matching Vector[x,y,z], Vector(x,y,z), [x,y,z], or (x,y,z), case-insensitive for Vector, and skips invalid entries.

Inserts the input element before the specified index in the selected List mode. Index 0 inserts at the beginning and -1 inserts before the last element. Indexes above the List size insert at the end, while indexes below the negative range insert at the beginning.
Returns a new List containing elements that are present in both input Lists.

Keeps only the elements of the selected List mode (Entity, Item or Block) whose display name matches the pattern. Names are the same as Selector: Display Name: a player's name, the custom name of an entity or item, and otherwise the name in the caster's language, so that last kind can give different results for casters with different languages. * matches any text, ? one character, and [abc] one of the listed characters. The whole name must match and case matters; use *Zombie* for a partial match.

Removes the elements of the selected List mode (Entity, Item or Block) whose display name matches the pattern. Names are the same as Selector: Display Name: a player's name, the custom name of an entity or item, and otherwise the name in the caster's language, so that last kind can give different results for casters with different languages. * matches any text, ? one character, and [abc] one of the listed characters. The whole name must match and case matters; use *Zombie* for a partial match.

Keeps the elements of the selected List mode (Entity, Item or Block) whose number at the NBT Path is between Min and Max, both included; an unconnected bound is open. Only number values count, as in the Number mode of Selector: NBT Value, so elements without one are dropped. If the path reaches several numbers, one in range is enough. To compare: at least a = Min a; at most a = Max a; equal to a = Min and Max both a.

Keeps the elements of the selected List mode whose number at the NBT Path is below Min or above Max; with neither connected, nothing is out of range. Elements without a number are dropped, as in Operator: List Keep NBT In Range. If the path reaches several numbers, one out of range is enough. To compare: greater than a = Max a; less than a = Min a; not equal to a = Min and Max both a.

Keeps the elements of the selected List mode (Entity, Item or Block) whose NBT value at the NBT Path matches the pattern. Values become text as in the String mode of Selector: NBT Value, and the whole text must match (* ? [abc], case kept). If the path reaches several values, one match is enough; elements where it reaches nothing are not kept. Unlike Operator: List Keep Matches, there is no namespace rule and no # tags.

Removes the elements of the selected List mode (Entity, Item or Block) whose NBT value at the NBT Path matches the pattern. Values become text as in the String mode of Selector: NBT Value, and the whole text must match (* ? [abc], case kept). If the path reaches several values, one match is enough; elements where it reaches nothing are kept. Unlike Operator: List Remove Matches, there is no namespace rule and no # tags.
Removes up to two elements from the List.

Removes the elements at Number A and Number B from the selected List mode. Negative indexes count from the end, so -1 removes the last element. Both indexes are resolved against the original List, and duplicate indexes remove only one element. An out-of-range index raises an out-of-bounds spell error.
Keeps elements in the selected List matching the pattern (* ? [abc]).$(p)Entity, Item, and Block match by ID, or by tag when starting with # (e.g., #minecraft:logs).
Removes elements in the selected List matching the pattern (* ? [abc]).$(p)Entity, Item, and Block match by ID, or by tag when starting with # (e.g., #minecraft:logs).
Outputs the number of elements in the List.

Returns a selected range of elements from the selected List mode as a new List. If A is omitted, the range starts at the beginning; if B is omitted, it continues to the end. Negative numbers count from the end, out-of-range values are clamped to the valid range, and an end position at or before the start returns an empty List. Decimal values are truncated toward zero.

Converts an Any input into a String List using the same display-oriented text form as Trick: Debug. Contextual values such as Entity, Item, and Block therefore use their debug display text rather than registry IDs. List inputs, including Block List, convert each element by the same rules while preserving order. Non-list inputs become a one-element String List.

Sorts the elements of the selected List mode by Values, smallest first, and returns the element at the Number. Counting starts at 0, and a negative Number counts from the largest, so -1 is the element with the largest value. Equal values keep the List's order. A Number outside the List, or Lists of different sizes, is an error.

Sorts the elements of the selected List mode by Values and keeps some of them, like Operator: List Keep By Distance. A positive Number keeps that many with the smallest values, a negative Number the largest, and 0 gives an empty List. Lists other than Entity come out smallest first (largest first for a negative Number); an Entity List keeps Psi's own order. Equal values keep the List's order. If the sizes differ, the spell fails with an error.

Keeps the elements of the selected List mode whose value is between Min and Max, both included. Values is a Number List with one value per element, in the same order, such as the output of Selector: NBT Number List. An unconnected Min or Max does not limit that side. The order of the List is kept. If the sizes differ, the spell fails with an error.
Adds matrices of the same size. The optional third matrix is added after the second.

Builds a 4×4 matrix from the caster's axis-rounded right, up, and forward directions plus an origin (the caster's block if omitted), in 2D, 3D, or Face mode.$(p)Left-multiply a region around (0, 0, 0) via Operator: Matrix Multiply to orient it with the caster.
Returns the number of columns as a Number.
Converts a Number List or Vector into a column matrix. The input must contain 1 to 4 elements.

Builds an axis-aligned 4×4 cuboid matrix from opposite corners Vector A and Vector B. Default Block mode includes both corner blocks; Vector mode uses the raw points.$(p)Pass to zone tricks, Operator: Inside Region, or Operator: Region Vector List.

Builds a 4x4 matrix that defines an axis-aligned cuboid centered at the input position. Whole-number size components are treated as block counts around the block that contains the input position: odd counts are centered on that block, positive even counts include one extra block in the positive direction, and negative even counts include one extra block in the negative direction. Non-integer components keep continuous edge lengths. Pass the matrix to Operator: Region Vector List to turn the region into block coordinates before using Trick: Mass Block Break. In Number mode the Size is one number used for all three axes, so a Size of 5 makes a 5x5x5 cube.
Deletes the column at the zero-based index from the matrix. The matrix must have at least 2 columns so that the result is not empty.
Deletes the row at the zero-based index from the matrix. The matrix must have at least 2 rows so that the result is not empty.
Computes the determinant. The matrix must be square.
Creates a diagonal matrix from a Number List or Vector. The input must contain 1 to 4 elements.
Returns the element at (row, column) using zero-based indexes.
Returns the column at the zero-based index as a Number List.
Returns the row at the zero-based index as a Number List.
Flattens the matrix into a Number List in row-major order.
Creates an identity matrix of the given size. The size must be 1 to 4.
Computes the inverse matrix. The matrix must be square and have a non-zero determinant.
Extracts the top-left 3x3 part of the matrix. Matrices smaller than 3x3 cause an error.
Multiplies matrices from left to right. The columns of each matrix must match the rows of the next.
Treats the Vector or Number List as a column vector and multiplies it by the matrix on the left.
Replaces the specified column with a Number List or Vector. Missing rows are filled with zero, and specifying a column beyond the current size expands the matrix with zeros.
Replaces the element at the zero-based [row, column] indices with the input number. The indices list must contain exactly two numbers.
Replaces the specified row with a Number List or Vector. Missing columns are filled with zero, and specifying a row beyond the current size expands the matrix with zeros.

Builds a 4x4 matrix that rotates around Axis, through the origin, by Angle in radians, the same rotation as Operator: Rotate Vector. Quarter turns come out exact, so rotated regions keep their block positions. A zero axis is an error.

To rotate around a point P instead, chain two Operator: Matrix Multiply pieces to get (translation by P) × (this matrix) × (translation by -P), making the translations with Operator: Translation Matrix.
Returns the number of rows as a Number.
Multiplies every element of the matrix by the input number.
Rotates a region matrix around its center so its Y axis points along Direction.$(p)Useful for aiming Trick: Gravity Zone in Matrix mode.
Subtracts matrices of the same size. The optional third matrix is subtracted after the second.
Transforms a vector with a 3x3 or 4x4 matrix. A 3x3 matrix multiplies [x,y,z]. A 4x4 matrix treats the vector as a homogeneous point [x,y,z,1] and divides the result by w.

Modes: Vector transforms one vector. Vector List transforms each vector of a Vector List and returns them in the same order; if any of them cannot be transformed, such as when w becomes 0, it is an error. A Block List also works; its block positions are used.

Builds a 4x4 matrix that moves points by Offset. Put it to the left of a region matrix in Operator: Matrix Multiply to move the region, or apply it with Operator: Matrix Transform Vector to move a position. With Operator: Rotation Matrix, it rotates a region around any point.
Swaps rows and columns of the matrix.
Creates a zero matrix. If the second size is omitted, a square matrix is returned.
Converts a Number List with exactly three elements into a Vector. The list order is X, Y, Z. If the list does not contain exactly three elements, the spell raises a runtime error.

Filters a list and returns only the elements outside the parallelepiped defined by a 3x4 or 4x4 matrix. The first three columns are the edge vectors and the fourth column is the start point. Points exactly on the boundary are counted as inside, so they are excluded.

Choose the list type in the mode menu. Entity (default) tests the center of each bounding box, Vector tests each vector as given, and Block tests block positions, the same points Operator: Region Vector List returns.
Outputs the player's name when the input Entity is a player. Non-player entities output an empty String.
Returns one random element from the input List.

Returns all block position vectors inside a 3D parallelepiped defined by a 3x4 or 4x4 matrix. The first three columns are the edge vectors and the fourth column is the start point. Vectors are returned in fixed local u, v, and w order. The operator does not inspect the world, so air, unloaded chunks, and unbreakable blocks are not filtered. The returned Vector List can be passed to Trick: Mass Block Break. Regions above the shared internal limit raise an error.
Returns the hyperbolic sine of the target number.

Turns an Item, or every item of an Item List, into a strict Item. Connect it to an item filter, such as the filter of Trick: Ideaspace Storage - Deposit/Withdraw, the Slot tricks, or the Item modes of Trick: Pull Item and Trick: Send Item, to match only items with the same data components, such as enchantments, durability and names. The count is never compared. An empty Item is an error; empty elements of a list are skipped.
Concatenates String 1, String 2, and optional String 3 in that order.
Outputs 1 if String 1 ends with String 2, otherwise outputs 0. The comparison is case-sensitive.
Returns the number of characters in the input String.
Joins the input String List with String 2 and outputs a String. If String 2 is not connected, a comma is used. Empty delimiters are allowed and concatenate the elements directly.

Searches String 1 with String 2 and checks whether it contains matching text. * matches any text, ? matches one character, and [abc] matches one of the listed characters. Escape wildcard characters with a backslash. Matching is case-sensitive.

Replaces every literal, case-sensitive occurrence of String 2 in String 1 with String 3. String 2 is evaluated only as an exact match. If String 2 is empty, String 1 is returned unchanged. The result is limited by the runtime String length limit.

Returns a selected range of characters from the input String as a new String. If A or B is not connected, the beginning or end is used. Negative numbers count from the end, out-of-range values are clamped to the valid range, and an end position at or before the start returns an empty String. Decimal values are truncated toward zero.
Splits String 1 with String 2 as the delimiter and outputs a String List. If String 2 is not connected, a comma is used. Empty fields are preserved.
Outputs 1 if String 1 starts with String 2, otherwise outputs 0. The comparison is case-sensitive.
Removes whitespace characters (such as spaces, tabs, and line breaks) from the beginning and end of the input String. Whitespace inside the String is preserved.
Raycasts from Position in the Ray direction and returns the position of the first block hit. Blocks without a collision shape are ignored.
Raycasts from Position in the Ray direction and returns the normal direction of the face of the first block with a collision shape hit.
Outputs registry tags from a Contextual Value as a String List. Entries use namespace:path form without #. Entity inputs return EntityType tags, not scoreboard tags.
Returns the tangent of the target number.
Returns the hyperbolic tangent of the target number.

Converts an Any input into a String using the same display-oriented text form as Trick: Debug. Contextual values such as Entity, Item, and Block therefore use their debug display text rather than registry IDs. String values are returned as-is. List values convert each element by the same rules and join them with commas.
Converts a Vector into a Number List with three elements in X, Y, Z order.
Raycasts from Position in the Ray direction and returns the position of the first block hit. Water and lava can stop the ray.
Raycasts from Position in the Ray direction and returns the normal direction of the face of the first block or fluid hit.
psi.book.page.psitweaks_spellpiece.safet: It works effectively no matter where it is placed within the program. Immediately before Psi is consumed, it compares the spell’s actual Psi consumption with the total of the caster’s current Psi and the Psi in the CAD battery. If the caster’s Psi is insufficient, the spell is canceled without consuming any Psi.
psi.book.page.psitweaks_spellpiece.selec: Outputs the center of the $(thing)Autonomous Caster$(0) block casting the spell, as a Vector. The Autonomous Caster's caster is in front of the machine, so the position of $(thing)Selector: Caster$(0) is the block in front. It fails when cast from anything but an Autonomous Caster.
Outputs the shield points the target's $(thing)Trick: Barrier$(0) has left, as a Number. It outputs 0 when the target has no shield or is not a living entity.

Outputs the block at the target position as a Block value. Block is a read-only snapshot containing the saved position, dimension, block state, registry ID, and block tags. Pieces that take a Block also accept a Vector directly, so this is mainly for viewing Block information with Trick: Debug.
Gets the blocks at the positions in a Vector List as a Block List. Use this when you want to handle positions as blocks, such as when searching a list by block type.

Outputs the display name of a Contextual Value as a String in the caster's current language. Players and custom-named entities keep their visible names; other entities use their EntityType name, Items use their hover name, and Blocks use their block name. If the caster's language or a translation is missing, English is used, then the translation key itself.

Outputs display names from a Contextual Value List as a String List while preserving input order. Entity List, Item List, and Block List are supported. Vector List input is converted to Block List by reading the blocks at those world coordinates. Each element uses the same language fallback as Selector: Display Name.

Outputs the registry ID of each active Mob Effect on the target Entity as a String List, including the namespace (for example, minecraft:speed). Non-living entities and living entities without active effects output an empty String List.

Outputs the Item in the target Entity's zero-based inventory slot. Players use their player inventory; other entities use their item handler when available. Unreadable, empty, negative, or out-of-range slots output an empty Item.

Outputs the item registered in the given slot (1 to 9) of the caster's Filter Card in use, as an Item value with a count of 1. Connect it to Operator: Strict Item to also match data such as enchantments and names.$(p)If the caster has no Filter Card, or the slot is empty, the spell stops with an error.

Outputs the target living entity's main-hand ItemStack as an Item value: a read-only snapshot of its kind, count, durability, name and so on. A dropped item, such as from Psi's Selector: Nearby Items, gives its own stack.

Outputs carried items from the target Entity as an Item List. Player inventories are read slot by slot; other entities use their item handler when available, or their hands and armor slots as a fallback. Empty inventories output an empty Item List, and a dropped item a list of its own stack.

Returns how much of a resource your Ideaspace Storage holds as a Number (count for items, mB for fluids and chemicals, FE for FE).$(p)Takes an ID String or Item for items, an ID String for fluids and chemicals, and no input for FE. Items and fluids with the same ID are summed across data components.

Returns how much more of a resource your Ideaspace Storage can accept as a Number, returning 0 for a new type when the type limit is full.$(p)Takes an ID String or Item (including data) for items, an ID String for fluids and chemicals, and no input for FE.

Returns the amount actually moved by the most recent Ideaspace transfer trick earlier in the same cast, or 0 if none ran or moved nothing.$(p)Because tricks run from top left, connect this selector to tricks placed after the transfer.

Returns the number of types of one resource kind currently stored in your Ideaspace Storage, as a Number. The mode picks Item (I), Fluid (F) or Chemical (C). Items and fluids with different data components count as separate types, as in the storage's type limit.

Outputs the element at a zero-based index from the input List. Negative indexes count back from the end: -1 returns the last element, and -2 returns the element before it. Out-of-range indexes produce the same out-of-bounds spell error as Psi's Indexed Element.
Outputs items from the target block's internal inventory as an Item List. Item handlers and containers are read slot by slot. Blocks without readable inventories output an empty Item List.

Outputs the Item in the target block's zero-based internal inventory slot. Item handlers are used first, with Container as a fallback. Blocks without a readable inventory and empty, negative, or out-of-range slots output an empty Item.

Outputs the entries of the compound or list at the NBT Path as a String List: "key:value" for a compound, sorted by key, and "index:value" for a list, with values as SNBT. Unconnected or empty, the whole NBT is read. Any other value, a missing path or a target without NBT gives an empty List. Paths work as in Selector: NBT Value.

Outputs 1 if the NBT Path reaches anything in the target's NBT, otherwise 0. Paths work as in Selector: NBT Value, so it also tells whether a list has an element or whether a filter such as Inventory[{Slot:0b}] matches. A target without NBT, such as a block without a block entity, gives 0.

Outputs the keys of the compound at the NBT Path, sorted, or the indexes "0", "1", ... of a list, as a String List. Unconnected or empty, the top-level keys are given. Any other value or a missing path gives an empty List. Paths work as in Selector: NBT Value.

Reads every element of the selected List mode (Entity, Item or Block) as Selector: NBT Value does in Number mode and outputs the numbers as a Number List in the List's order (an Entity List is in Psi's own order), so the two line up. An element without a number at the NBT Path gives the Fallback, or 0. Example: with the NBT Path Health, Operator: List Keep By Value with -1 keeps the entity with the most health.

Reads NBT from an entity, item, or block using command NBT path syntax (e.g., Inventory[0].id) and returns the first match.$(p)String mode returns values as text, while Number mode returns numbers only. Missing values or invalid paths never error, returning Fallback (empty String or 0 if unset).
Gets SpellGram objects (Resident SpellGrams, Meteor Lines, and Micro Black Holes) around the specified coordinates. It is mainly used by tricks that control placed SpellGram objects.
Outputs the names of all online players in the caster's current world as a String List.

Lists the Resident SpellGrams (circles and zones) you placed in this dimension, however far away they are, oldest first. An Autonomous Caster gets only the ones it placed itself. A Meteor Line is not a Resident SpellGram and is not included.

Outputs the ItemStack in the slot selected by the spell as an Item value. This is the same slot used by Psi pieces such as Trick: Place Block, and is affected by Trick: Switch Target Slot. Empty slots output an empty Item.

Returns the current integrity of a SpellGram object (Resident SpellGram, Meteor Line, or Micro Black Hole) as a Number.$(p)Matches the integrity shown when aiming at the core, useful before Trick: Extend SpellGram.

Returns the current integrity of every SpellGram object in the List as a Number List, in the List's order (an Entity List is in Psi's own order), so it can be the Values of Operator: Value-Ranked Element and the other value-ranked list operators. The numbers are the same as Selector: SpellGram Integrity. Any element that is not a SpellGram object is an error. Example: with Selector: Own Resident SpellGrams as the List, Operator: Value-Ranked Element with 0 picks your SpellGram with the least integrity for Trick: Extend SpellGram.
Gets an entity from the UUID stored in CAD memory. Only an entity within the spell's range is found.
Gets a Plain Value from CAD memory. Use the mode button to choose String, Number, or Vector. String conversions are strict; Number and Vector cannot be converted directly.
psi.book.page.psitweaks_spellpiece.trick: Accelerates crops, saplings, and other growing plants inside to (Power + 5) times normal speed. Block entities and living beings are unaffected.$(p)Also speeds up random block changes of your own overlapping zones by the same factor. See $(l:psitweaks/zone_magic)Zone Magic$(/l) for shared rules.
Creates a spherical shockwave at the specified coordinates and damages living beings within range.

Fires a bullet of compressed air from the position in the direction. The bullet's range is 24 blocks.$(br)A creature the bullet hits directly takes $(thing)4.5 + 4.5 × Power$(0) damage, and the bullet stops there. A graze from the pressure wave around the bullet deals a third of a direct hit's damage, and the bullet flies on.

Fires a water-blade projectile forward as an early-game offensive trick, dealing $(thing)2 + 3 × Power$(0) damage. A creature it hits stays wet for 10 seconds, as if in the rain: it does not catch fire, and $(thing)Trick: Chain Lightning$(0), $(thing)Trick: Burst$(0) and Thundercloud bolts deal it more. A burning creature takes 25%% more instead: the water turns to steam and puts out the fire, but the creature stays dry.

Wraps the target in a psionic shield worth $(thing)Power × 10$(0) points for one minute. While the shield lasts, damage the target takes comes off the shield instead of its health, and a honeycomb sphere flashes around it. Damage beyond what is left goes through, and the shield breaks.

Casting it again replaces the shield only if the new one is stronger. While shielded, the target does not catch fire. It does not absorb falling, drowning, poison and the like. A bar above your health shows the shield you have left and the seconds remaining.
Fires a ball of flame forward as an early-game offensive trick, dealing $(thing)2 + 2 × Power$(0) damage.
Breaks the target block with Fortune.
Breaks the target block with Silk Touch.
Feeds each target animal (an Entity, or every entity of an Entity List) a breeding food from the caster's inventory so that it falls in love. A warning names an animal the caster has no food for.
Babies, animals resting after breeding and others that cannot breed right now get no food. If any target is out of range, the spell fails.

Vaporizes the liquid inside the target, dealing $(thing)36 + 30 × Power$(0) damage that ignores armor and shields. Works on bosses too. Wet creatures take 1.25x damage.$(p)If the target dies from it, its body bursts and hits nearby hostile creatures for up to 40%% of the damage.

Discharges lightning from the focal point along $(thing)Direction$(0), striking the nearest hostile creature within 24 blocks. Chains to up to 3 hostile creatures within 8 blocks, then up to 2 more from each within 8 blocks.

Deals $(thing)9 + 9 × Power$(0) on the first hit, 40%% on the first chain, and 20%% on the second; wet creatures take 1.25x damage.$(p)Set optional $(thing)Indiscriminate$(0) to non-zero to also hit animals and villagers (sparing you, allies, and pets).

Distributes a Cost-based FE capacity evenly to FE blocks, entities, dropped items, and players carrying a Zone Receiver inside.$(p)Randomly scrapes oxidation off unwaxed copper, and with Applied Energistics 2 processes dropped items like a Charger. See $(l:psitweaks/zone_magic)Zone Magic$(/l) for shared rules.

Overlapping your Turbulence Zone creates a Thundercloud that strikes creatures below (1.25x damage on wet creatures) and boosts FE output. With Create, adding your Heat Zone enables bulk blasting.$(p)If your $(l:psitweaks_machines/zone_feeder)Zone Feeder$(/l) is inside, it supplies extra FE whenever the zone's own capacity runs short.
Keep this in your inventory inside a Charged Zone to charge your FE items. Right-click to toggle on or off; without it, carried items and gear are not charged.

Makes your circles (newest one if omitted) follow Follow Target every tick. Follow Target must be you or a non-living entity in range (such as a boat or item); omit it to detach.$(p)Zones cannot be moved. Moving consumes extra integrity, and detaches if the target vanishes or moves over 32 blocks from you.

Takes no input. Blows a blizzard in front of the caster (passing through blocks) and freezes the minds of the mobs it catches forever. A frozen mob's AI stops and it is sealed in ice, unable to move or make a sound.

Players, the caster, the caster's pets and allies, and bosses are not frozen. The blizzard itself deals no damage.$(br2)If something else turns a frozen mob's AI back on, the ice melts and the mob can make sounds again.

Exposes living beings inside to radiation every second up to a limit set by Power, leaving no radiation sources. Blocked by MekaSuit and Trick: Radiation Filter.$(p)Spares you, pets, and allies. See $(l:psitweaks/zone_magic)Zone Magic$(/l) for shared rules.
Opens a 3x3 crafting grid, as if the caster had used a crafting table, with no crafting table needed.
Removes the target's radiation exposure.

Deploys all swords in your $(l:items/psitweaks_blade_pouch)$(o)$(item)Blade Pouch$(0)$(/l) around you as spectral blades. They dart at hostile creatures within 16 blocks, slash them, and return, fading after 3 attacks or 15 seconds.

Each slash deals the sword's attack damage scaled by Phenomenon Interference and applies enchantments without consuming durability. Recasting redeploys the blades.$(p)Set optional $(thing)Indiscriminate$(0) to non-zero to also target animals and villagers (sparing you, allies, and pets).

Applies Torpor to living beings inside, heavily reducing movement and flying speed (and players' attack speed) according to Power. Spares you, pets, allies, and bosses.$(p)Also slows projectiles inside every tick (excluding magic projectiles). Does not cancel out Acceleration Zones. See $(l:psitweaks/zone_magic)Zone Magic$(/l) for shared rules.

Places a decontamination core at Position that weakens Mekanism radiation sources within 32 blocks every second. Does not reduce living beings' dose (use Trick: Cure Radiation).$(p)Takes Power and Time (default 30 s, max 120 s). See $(l:psitweaks/spellgram_objects)SpellGram Objects$(/l) for shared rules.
Behaves similarly to Psi's Trick: Die and refunds the Psi cost of spell pieces that were not executed. With high-frequency casting, the client-side Psi display may temporarily desync.
Removes effects from the target entity. This is the general-purpose dispel that does not distinguish between beneficial and harmful effects.
Removes only beneficial effects from the target entity. It is suited for stripping enhancements from hostile targets.
Removes non-beneficial effects from the target entity. Use it when you want to cleanse harmful effects while leaving allied buffs intact.

Fires a dry ice projectile forward, dealing $(thing)14$(0) freezing damage to targets it hits. The dry ice sublimates into carbon dioxide, inflicting Carbon Poisoning that impairs the target's mobility and deals damage over time.
Opens the caster's ender chest, with no ender chest block needed.
Creates an explosion that deals damage without destroying blocks. Dropped items and experience orbs are not erased by the blast.

Restores the integrity of your own Resident SpellGram given as the Target, however far away it is. Its cost is 100 per Power (a constant of at most 100). It gives back the share of the integrity the object had when placed that this cost is of what the object cost when placed, so costly objects are harder to restore. Integrity lost to spells comes back first. Integrity wears away at a steady rate, so anything restored beyond that makes the object last longer. Integrity can be restored up to a cap: twice what the object would have had if placed with the longest Time (120 seconds), whatever Time it was placed with.

Places a fire circle at Position that deals fire damage every 0.5 s and ignites creatures inside for 2 s (Time: default 60 s, max 120 s). Overlapping circles of your own apply only the strongest.$(p)Move it with Trick: Circle Follow or movement tricks. Pauses inside a stronger opposing Interference Zone. See $(l:psitweaks/spellgram_objects)SpellGram Objects$(/l) for shared rules.

Applies the Flight effect to the target. The Flight effect enables creative flight but consumes Psi every 0.5 seconds. The amount consumed varies based on the Flight effect level, the efficiency of the CAD used to apply the effect, and the spell bullet's cost multiplier. The base consumption at effect levels 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 or higher is 1000 / 750 / 500 / 250 / 5 Psi every 0.5 seconds, respectively.
Freezes the target block one stage. Water becomes ice, ice becomes packed ice, packed ice becomes blue ice, lava becomes magma block, and magma block becomes obsidian.

Chills living beings inside like Powder Snow according to Power, slowing and damaging them once frozen. Wet creatures freeze twice as fast, while you, pets, allies, and leather armor wearers are spared.$(p)Randomly freezes open water sources into ice. See $(l:psitweaks/zone_magic)Zone Magic$(/l) for shared rules.

With Mekanism installed, cools heat-holding blocks and machines inside using a Cost-based cooling total.$(p)When touching or overlapping your own Heat Zone, heat drawn from hot blocks is transferred into that Heat Zone's heat total.

Takes no input. Blasts every SpellGram object in front of the caster, removing $(thing)300$(0) times the caster's Phenomenon Interference from each one's integrity. Blocks do not stop it.$(br)Creatures in the same range take $(thing)6$(0) damage. The caster's own SpellGram objects are left alone.

Continuously pushes entities inside according to Power. Power 4 roughly balances gravity, and upward push prevents fall damage.$(p)With Create Aeronautics (Sable), also pushes and tilts Simulated Contraptions. See $(l:psitweaks/zone_magic)Zone Magic$(/l) for shared rules.

Default Vector mode pushes along Direction for 30 seconds. Matrix mode pushes along the Matrix's Y axis (reversed with negative Power) and accepts Time. Use Operator: Matrix Set Y Axis to aim in any direction.
Deals $(thing)24$(0) slash damage to the target and makes it drop a head when killed.
Applies a hardening effect that limits large incoming damage to a fixed value. Maximum damage taken is capped at (level - 2).
Harvests the ripe crop at the position and replants it with one of its seeds. The harvest goes into the caster's inventory. Cast from a Psimetal tool, the tool's Fortune applies.
Sweet berry bushes and glow berries are only picked. Sugar cane, cactus and bamboo keep their lowest block, and melons and pumpkins are taken while the stem stays. Unripe crops are left alone.
Harvests the crops in a line that starts at the position and runs $(thing)Max$(0) blocks in the direction of the target, the same way as $(thing)Trick: Harvest$(0).

Ignites living beings inside according to Power, sparing you, pets, allies, and wet creatures.$(p)Randomly melts Ice, Frosted Ice, and snow layers, and dries Wet Sponges. See $(l:psitweaks/zone_magic)Zone Magic$(/l) for shared rules.

Produces a Cost-based heat total that heats Create Blaze Burners without fuel and shares remaining heat with Mekanism heat blocks, plus heat transferred from your Freeze Zones.$(p)With Create installed, overlapping your Turbulence Zone bulk-smokes items, and adding your Charged Zone switches it to bulk-blasting.

Places an ice circle at Position that deals freezing damage and chills creatures inside every 0.5 s (Time: default 60 s, max 120 s). Overlapping circles of your own apply only the strongest.$(p)Move it with Trick: Circle Follow or movement tricks. Pauses inside a stronger opposing Interference Zone. See $(l:psitweaks/spellgram_objects)SpellGram Objects$(/l) for shared rules.

Turns open water sources inside into Frosted Ice and keeps them frozen (skips Heat Zones).$(p)While following via Trick: Circle Follow, freezes only on ground movement; ice/land boats freeze water ahead, while floating boats do not.

Deposits the chosen resource (Item, Fluid, Chemical, or FE) from the specified block face into your Ideaspace Storage, up to Number items, Power * 1000 mB, or Power * 4000 FE.$(p)Follows face I/O rules and errors on protected blocks; skips your own Ideaspace Connector except for FE.

The filter is optional and absent in FE mode. Fluid and Chemical modes match ID Strings with *, ?, and # tags.$(p)Item mode matches by ID or # tag via String, by type via Item or Item List, or by exact data via Operator: Strict Item.

Exact Transfer modes (I=, F=, C=) move the exact full amount of one resource type, or nothing at all without raising an error.$(p)Different types or data components are never combined; the first qualifying type is moved.

Deposits the item in the spell's target slot into your Ideaspace Storage, up to the count given by Number. Moves as much as fits.$(p)The filter is optional and uses the same matching rules as $(l:psitweaks_spell_pieces/trick_idea_storage_deposit)$(o)Trick: Ideaspace Storage - Deposit$(0)$(/l).
The target slot matches Psi's Trick: Place Block (default: right of the CAD) and can be changed with Trick: Switch Focus Slot.$(p)Skips the active CAD or casting tool slot.

Opens your personal Ideaspace Storage for items, fluids, Mekanism chemicals, and FE (default limits: 256 item, 64 fluid, and 64 chemical types).$(p)Left-click (right-click for 1) or Shift-click to store items. With an empty cursor, left-click withdraws a stack and right-click takes half.

Right-click with a fluid or chemical container to store or fill it (hold Shift to repeat). Left-click a fluid with an empty cursor to fill a stored empty bucket.$(p)The side crafting button opens a 3x3 grid that auto-refills ingredients from storage, with search, sorting, and JEI/EMI recipe transfer.

Withdraws the chosen resource (Item, Fluid, Chemical, or FE) from your Ideaspace Storage into the specified block face, up to Number items, Power * 1000 mB, or Power * 4000 FE.$(p)Filters and Exact Transfer match $(l:psitweaks_spell_pieces/trick_idea_storage_deposit)$(o)Trick: Ideaspace Storage - Deposit$(0)$(/l); multiple matches are withdrawn in turn up to the limit.

Withdraws items from your Ideaspace Storage into the spell's target slot, up to the count given by Number. Fills up to the item's max stack size.$(p)Occupied slots only top up with identical data; empty slots take the first type matching the filter. Filter rules match $(l:psitweaks_spell_pieces/trick_idea_storage_deposit)$(o)Trick: Ideaspace Storage - Deposit$(0)$(/l).
The target slot matches Psi's Trick: Place Block (default: right of the CAD) and can be changed with Trick: Switch Focus Slot.$(p)Skips the active CAD or casting tool slot.

Places an Ideaspace Connector linked to your Ideaspace Storage. It never expires, and breaking it keeps storage intact.$(p)Incoming resources go straight to storage; right-click to publish up to 9 resources for extraction. Works offline while chunk-loaded.

All six faces default to I/O enabled with automatic export off. Face I/O, redstone rules, export rate and interval, and stock limits can be overridden per published slot.$(p)The Input filter restricts accepted resources across all faces; FE is always accepted.

Use Copy and Paste on the main page to transfer published slots, face settings, stock limits, and input filters as JSON between connectors.$(p)Removing sections leaves those parts unchanged, and faces keep their world directions.
Acts on the target block as if right-clicked with the item in the caster's off hand.

Stops other casters with lower Phenomenon Interference from running tricks or placing zones inside. Does not affect you, your Autonomous Casters, or other mods' magic.$(p)Also blocks non-caster ender teleports into or out of the area. See $(l:psitweaks/zone_magic)Zone Magic$(/l) for shared rules.

Jumps forward to the next Jump Anchor with the same label when the target number is unset, or when its absolute value is less than 1. The label input is optional, but if used it must be a String constant. Empty labels only match empty-label anchors. It cannot jump to Jump Anchors behind it.

Uses the same conditions as Trick: Jump to jump to a Jump Anchor, then refunds the Psi cost of the spell pieces actually skipped by the jump. With high-frequency casting, the client-side Psi display may temporarily desync.

Breaks blocks at the coordinates in a Vector List or Block List, up to the limit (positive integer constant, max 4096), counting duplicates once.$(p)Drops go into the caster's inventory, with overflow dropping at the caster's position.
Harvests the crops at the first $(thing)Max$(0) coordinates (at most 4096) in a Vector List (a Block List also works), the same way as $(thing)Trick: Harvest$(0).
If any position is out of range, the spell fails before harvesting anything. The crops are harvested a little at a time, and the caster gets the whole harvest at the end.
Breaks specific blocks and transmutes them into other items. The Material Mutator can perform this process using power and Vaporized Psionic Echo.
Melts the target block one stage. Ice, packed ice, and blue ice become water; obsidian, stone-like blocks, and cobblestone-like blocks become magma block; and magma block becomes lava.

Spreads a sphere of night around the position, with a radius of $(thing)Radius$(0) blocks (16 to 32, 16 if left out). Stars light up in its upper half, and after one second they rain streaks of light for one second: at least one at every creature inside that the spell may harm, and the rest onto the ground.

A streak passes through blocks without breaking them, so a roof gives no cover, and deals lethal damage to whatever it touches. Creatures outside the night when a streak falls are not aimed at. The caster, their pets and allies are never hit.

Creates a micro black hole at the position. For 10 seconds it drags creatures within $(thing)Radius$(0) blocks (16 to 32) and swings them around its centre at speed; a creature whipping past the centre may be flung out of range. In the last 1.5 seconds it swallows them, then collapses and crushes everything within three tenths of $(thing)Radius$(0) of the centre.
The collapse deals $(thing)30 + 25 × Power$(0) damage that ignores armor and shields, falling to half at the edge.

Strikes the ground at the position so a shockwave ring spreads out to $(thing)Radius$(0) blocks (2 to 12). Everything standing on the ground when the ring passes takes damage and is thrown into the air; anything already in the air is unharmed. The position must be within 3 blocks above the ground.$(p)Damage is $(thing)16 + 12 × Power$(0) at the centre and falls to 40%% at the edge.
Cuts living beings along a plane defined by three points, dealing $(thing)60 × Power$(0) damage.

Conjures a lookalike of the caster at the position, which wanders around it. It wavers away after $(thing)Time$(0) seconds or after taking $(thing)2 × Power$(0) hits. Casting it again replaces the current lookalike.

While it stands, hostile creatures within 32 blocks that go for the caster go for the lookalike instead (bosses excepted). Other players no longer see the caster, and their spells aimed at the caster go to the lookalike and never reach the caster. Team mates are unaffected.
Fires a high-power heat ray using ultrasonic vibration, dealing $(thing)2 × Power$(0) damage per tick.
Raycasts from the specified position in the Ray direction; if it hits a Simulated Contraption, applies propulsion to it.

Calls down Number pseudo meteors (max 16) around the position, homing in on nearby hostile creatures in order or landing near the position.$(p)Set optional Indiscriminate to non-zero to also target animals and villagers (sparing you, allies, and pets).
Explodes on impact for up to $(thing)25 + 20 × Power$(0) damage and 3 s of fire. Passes through terrain without breaking blocks and is reduced by Blast Protection.

Fires a bullet of psions from the position in the direction. The bullet's range is 24 blocks, and it stops at the first creature, SpellGram object or block it hits.$(br)A creature it hits takes $(thing)2 + Power$(0) damage. When it hits the core of a SpellGram object, it removes $(thing)8 + 2 × Power$(0) times the caster's Phenomenon Interference from that object's integrity. It flies through the caster's own SpellGram objects.

Pulls up to one stack (capped by optional Max) from the specified face of the block into your inventory.$(p)Filter modes: String (ID, *, or # tag), Item, and data-matching Item (Strict). Item modes also accept an Item List.

Generates a magical Pulsar block at Position. The block emits a redstone signal with strength 15 in every direction and glows in the color of the caster's CAD. If Time is positive, it disappears after that many ticks; if Time is omitted or zero or less, it remains until broken.

Generates a non-solid Pulsar light at Position. The light emits a redstone signal with strength 15 in every direction. Its color reflects the color of the caster's CAD. If Time is positive, it disappears after that many ticks; if Time is omitted or zero or less, it remains until broken.

Constructs solid Pulsars in a straight line from Position in the direction of Target. The number generated is limited by the lesser of the length of the Target vector and Max. Each Pulsar emits a redstone signal with strength 15. If Time is positive, they disappear after that many ticks; if Time is omitted or zero or less, they remain until broken.
Applies a radiation protection effect to the target.

Ends your own Resident SpellGrams given as the Target (an entity or a list, such as Selector: Own Resident SpellGrams), however far away they are. If anything else is in the target, nothing is ended and the spell errors. Psi is not refunded.

Moves items from the caster's inventory into the inventory of the block at the target position, through the specified face. Only one stack is moved per cast; if the destination cannot hold it all, only what fits is moved. CADs are never moved.

The filter modes and the optional Max input behave like Trick: Pull Item, including Item Lists in both Item modes. Casting fails with an error if the block has no inventory, no matching item is held, or the block is protected.
Shears the target, an Entity or every entity of an Entity List, as if the caster had used shears on it. Mobs from other mods that shears work on are sheared too.
What comes off goes into the caster's inventory. Targets that cannot be sheared right now are skipped, and if any target is out of range, the spell fails.

Draws the outline of a region defined by a 3x4 or 4x4 matrix with particle trails in your CAD's color, to check it before working on it. Block mode (default) wraps the blocks that Operator: Region Vector List picks from the region; Vector mode draws the parallelepiped exactly as defined.

Time is an optional constant and works like the Time of Trick: Particle Trail: 20 by default, at most 1200, and it must be positive. Every corner must be within the spell radius, or casting fails with an error. Players near you see the particles too.

Silences sounds made inside and blocks vibrations like wool.$(p)Sculk Sensors, Sculk Shriekers, and Wardens cannot detect blocked vibrations, and Shriekers inside will not shriek. See $(l:psitweaks/zone_magic)Zone Magic$(/l) for shared rules.

Keeps living beings inside soaked and prevents fire. Extinguishes fire, campfires, and candles, hardens concrete powder, moistens farmland, and wets Sponges.$(p)With Create installed, bulk-washes items where your own Turbulence Zone overlaps (Rainstorm). See $(l:psitweaks/zone_magic)Zone Magic$(/l) for shared rules.
Stores the target entity's UUID in CAD memory.

Stores a Plain Value in CAD memory. The memory slot uses Psi's standard numbering: 1 is the first slot. Number, Vector, and String values overwrite each other in the same slot. String values longer than 128 characters are truncated when stored, and a warning is shown in the caster's chat.
Supplies FE to the target block. When CAD Efficiency is 100, it supplies 80 FE per Psi.
Infusion-converts Echo Shards into Psionic Echo.

Evaluates the input String and jumps forward to the next Jump Anchor whose constant label is equal to it. If no matching anchor exists ahead, it does not error and simply continues to the next spell piece, so place the default branch immediately after the Switch. It cannot jump to Jump Anchors behind it.

Uses the same conditions as Trick: Switch to jump to a Jump Anchor, then refunds the Psi cost of the spell pieces actually skipped by the jump. If no matching anchor exists, execution continues and no Psi is refunded. With high-frequency casting, the client-side Psi display may temporarily desync.
Multiplies the target block's tick progression by (2 ^ power). The upper limit is 512x speed. Casting it again on the same block replaces both the rate and the remaining time.

Blows a gale that deflects others' projectiles (excluding magic projectiles) according to Power, and disperses lingering potion and dragon's breath clouds. See $(l:psitweaks/zone_magic)Zone Magic$(/l) for shared rules.

Overlapping your own zones upgrades them into storms: Heat Zone becomes a Heat Storm, Freeze Zone a Blizzard, Soak Zone a Rainstorm, and Charged Zone a Thundercloud, boosting their attacks and output.$(p)With Create installed, Heat Storms bulk-smoke, adding Charged Zone bulk-blasts, and Rainstorms bulk-wash, scaling with turbulence.

Generates wind scaled by area, Power, and Phenomenon Interference.$(p)Mekanism Generators Wind Generators and Immersive Engineering Windmills with a Kinetic Dynamo inside share this wind to generate power, even indoors or obstructed.
psi.book.page.psitweaks_zone_magic.0: Zone Magic places $(l:psitweaks/spellgram_objects)Resident SpellGrams$(/l) that keep working inside an area, such as Gravity, Heat, and Freeze Zones.$(p)Zone tricks are unlocked by research (Program: Zone Magic for the basic zones, and dedicated programs for specialized zones). See $(l:psitweaks/spellgram_objects)SpellGram Objects$(/l) for shared integrity, limit, and management rules, and each piece's entry for its specific effects.
psi.book.page.psitweaks_zone_magic.1: Area is set by Matrix and Size (constant, max 16); omitting Matrix centers a cube on the caster. Preview areas with Trick: Show Region. Time is a constant up to 120 seconds (default 30).$(p)Power is a constant of at least 1. Gravity, Acceleration, Deceleration, and Contamination Zones cap at 10; Heat, Freeze, Turbulence, and Charged Zones accept higher Power to raise Cost and resource totals.
psi.book.page.psitweaks_zone_magic.2: Overlapping your own matching zones adds heat, cooling, FE, and wind totals while applying only the strongest of other effects. Gravity Zones add pushes, Heat and Freeze Zones cancel where they overlap, and your Turbulence Zone upgrades other zones into storms.$(p)Where different casters' zones overlap, only the owner with higher Phenomenon Interference when placed takes effect.
psi.book.page.psitweaks_zone_magic.3: Heat, cooling, FE, and wind are zone-wide totals determined by Cost and shared by everything inside.$(p)Processing and output speed for other mods' machines scales with Phenomenon Interference, and Create bulk processing only works where your own Turbulence Zone overlaps. With Create Aeronautics (Sable), zones also affect Simulated Contraptions.
